newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee auctions should now increase - ABIC.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee auctions should now increase - ABIC.

text.p: A complete sell-out at today's auction of 120,100 60-kg bags of Brazilian government coffee stocks should be a clear sign that the government needs to raise the size of its sales, a roaster representative said.

"The next auction should be a minimum of 200,000 bags and from March onwards, sales should be much bigger," said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (ABIC) which represents roasters.

Monthly Brazilian auctions for the 1996/97 coffee year (July/June) currently have a limit of 200,000 bags. Today's sale was in fact the largest so far, reflecting the decreasing availability of coffee from the 1996/97 harvest.

Exporters as well as domestic roasters have been pressing the government to make known its position on larger auctions, fearing tight supply, particularly in the April to June quarter, which would hit exports.
"What Brazil cannot lose out on is overseas sales," Nahum said.
Prices in the auction ranged up to 135.11 reais ($130) a bag which also reflected the good demand.
"Given there is a shortage of coffee, the prices were what they should be," Nahum said.
A top government coffee official expressed the government's satisfaction with today's result but would not be drawn on whether auctions would now start to see a substantial increase.
"It was a very good auction, we were hoping for a positive result," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"We will examine whether to raise sales. But it will depend on the market situation," he said.
